summary: This is a marketing landing page for 'Nimbus', a project tracking and collaboration tool. It highlights core product capabilities with a hero section featuring a Kanban board preview and a supporting three-column feature card grid.

stack.name: Next.js (App Router)
stack.why: Enables fast static page generation, server-rendered components, and built-in API routing.

stack.name: Tailwind CSS
stack.why: Provides utility-first classes to precisely implement measured design tokens and responsive layouts.

stack.name: Node.js + Prisma
stack.why: Provides lightweight ORM access to persist trial signups and lead demo requests.

stack.name: PostgreSQL (Neon)
stack.why: Serverless relational database with a generous free tier for storing users and demo leads.

stack.name: Vercel
stack.why: Zero-configuration deployment platform natively optimized for Next.js applications.

behaviour: Clicking 'Start free trial' opens a modal or redirects to a registration/onboarding flow with email capture.
Clicking 'Book a demo' displays a calendar picker (e.g. Calendly embed) or lead submission form.
Navigation links (Features, Pricing, Customers, Docs) scroll smoothly to corresponding anchor sections or navigate to destination pages.
Kanban board elements can have subtle hover animations to simulate interactable task cards.
Mobile viewport renders a hamburger menu button to reveal header links.
data: Feature item content: title, description, and icon identifiers.
User session data: authenticated status determining whether 'Log in' changes to 'Go to Dashboard'.
Lead submission payload: email, intent ('trial' or 'demo'), and timestamp.

backend.summary: Handles marketing lead capture, demo scheduling requests, and user authentication redirects.
backend.database: PostgreSQL hosted on Neon serverless for storing lead captures, newsletter subscriptions, and account metadata.
backend.auth: Public landing page with optional JWT / session cookies check to replace 'Log in' with 'Dashboard' if already logged in.

tables.name: leads
tables.columns: id uuid pk, email text unique, type text, source text, created_at timestamp

tables.name: demo_bookings
tables.columns: id uuid pk, lead_id uuid fk, company_name text, team_size int, scheduled_at timestamp

endpoints.purpose: Records a trial signup or email capture lead
Creates a demo request booking with company metadata
Health check for deployment uptime monitoring

rules: Email addresses must be structurally valid and lowercased before saving.
Duplicate lead emails should update the last activity timestamp rather than failing.

pitfalls: Using raster images for the Kanban board illustration instead of CSS/SVG, leading to blurry rendering on high-DPI screens.
Failing to make the Kanban preview responsive, causing horizontal overflow on tablets and small screens.
Hardcoding colors that deviate from the design system tokens instead of using Tailwind config palette extensions.
testing: Verify Hero title, badge text, and body copy render accurately via Playwright or React Testing Library.
Check that the Kanban board card accents display the correct blue, amber, and green left-border styles.
Ensure the '/api/leads' route rejects requests missing valid email formats with a 400 status code.
Verify layout collapses gracefully from multi-column grid to single-column on viewport widths below 768px.
deploy: Push codebase to a GitHub repository.
Import repository into Vercel, configure environment variables (DATABASE_URL), and trigger automatic production deployment.
Connect a custom domain with SSL enabled automatically by Vercel.

tokens.method: Colours: pixel quantisation of the whole screenshot and of each detected element. Font sizes: text box height ÷ 1.25. Spacing: gaps between sibling boxes, snapped to a 4px grid. Measured approximations, not values read from source code.
